corpus_invariants.why: The corpus is the persistent AST contract, so a defect recorded there as the expected result is invisible to every gate at once. A case whose expected tree holds fewer op_result nodes than its input has binding lines was accepted from --update without being read. The count is conservative: one line may bind several results.

invariants.why: The blocking examples gate already covers this. The probe adds the location, so a failure is actionable without re-parsing by hand.

op_result is on the Public AST Surface. A line that binds SSA results must produce the binding node; if it does not, the result definition was either dropped or re-attributed to a neighbouring operation, and every def-use consumer is wrong there. A line whose right-hand side starts with % is an operand assignment inside an operation's own syntax (a wrapped iter_args or gpu.launch header), not a binding, and is not checked.

Distinguishing a block label from a successor reference is the external scanner's stated job. A line-initial label that yields no block_label node means the scanner lost the distinction and the block structure collapsed.

Principle 4, boundary-preserving, in machine-checkable form. A custom operation body may be parsed coarsely, but it must not extend across a line that binds a new SSA result: that line belongs to the next operation. For an operation with regions, only the rows after its last region closes are checked -- rows inside a region belong to nested operations, which are checked on their own. Deliberately narrow -- it only fires on result bindings, which are unambiguous operation starts.

normalizer.why: Generic form is MLIR's own answer to the program's structure. The grammar parses generic form precisely (principle 2), so parsing mlir-opt's output with the same grammar turns an IR-versus-CST comparison into CST-versus-CST, where the mapping is the identity. --split-input-file raises coverage from 99/150 to 126/150 because the upstream tests are full of `// -----` chunks. --no-implicit-module was measured and rejected: it drops coverage to 52/150.

counts.label: results bound
counts.why: Counts the SSA results bound, not op_result nodes: generic form prints `%a, %b = ...` as the one group `%0:2 = ...`. Grammar > reference is always a defect: the grammar bound a result MLIR does not see. Grammar < reference with a large gap is a strong bug signal.
counts.caveat: MLIR allows an operation's results to go unnamed and the printer then invents a name, so the reference side can legitimately hold a few more. A gap of one or two is usually that, not a defect -- confirm before reporting. This is a ranked lead generator, not a pass/fail gate.

counts.why: the implicit builtin.module wrapper and terminators the custom form elides
the implicit module wrapper, and declarations that print an empty region
generic form materializes entry block labels the custom form omits

normalizer.also_accept_why: Any MLIR-based project's opt tool parses core MLIR and prints generic form, so any of them serves as the reference for the shared syntax. A downstream one additionally registers its own dialects, which raises how many files it accepts. Order is preference, not requirement; --tool overrides all of them.
normalizer.tool_is_declared_not_discovered: The reference parser is never searched for. `opt` on PATH is LLVM's IR optimiser, not an MLIR tool, and an arbitrary mlir-opt build may not register the dialects this repository needs -- either would yield a comparison that looks authoritative while resting on a binary nobody chose. The user declares it with --tool; probe.py then round-trips a trivial function through it and refuses if that fails.
normalizer.accepted_tools_for_reference: Any MLIR-based project's opt tool: mlir-opt, circt-opt, triton-opt, iree-opt, tpp-opt and so on. They all parse core MLIR and print generic form, which is the only part this comparison uses; a downstream one also registers its own dialects, which raises how many files it accepts.
